key_messages: Drier air finally will work its way into the region today with temperatures sharply warming through Thursday.
Shower chances return Thursday afternoon into Friday with localized breezy conditions, mainly in the St. Lawrence and Champlain Valleys.
Cooler than normal early next week with a slight threat of showers late Sunday-Monday.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
732 AM EDT Wed Sep 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 222 AM EDT Wednesday...

No changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 222 AM EDT Wednesday...

1. Drier air finally will work its way into the region today 
with temperatures sharply warming through Thursday. 

2. Shower chances return Thursday afternoon into Friday with 
localized breezy conditions, mainly in the St. Lawrence and 
Champlain Valleys. 

3. Cooler than normal early next week with a slight threat of 
showers late Sunday-Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 222 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Satellite this morning depicts widespread low stratus 
across the entire area with intermittent mist in the higher terrain, 
in association with lingering low level moisture evident on the GOES-
19 water vapor imagery. Blocked flow and a sharp inversion will 
likely keep these clouds and terrain mist/fog lingering through this 
morning, with froude numbers still well below 0.25. By this 
afternoon, model soundings show mid to upper level drying finally 
making it to the surface with froude number improving. Low clouds 
look to break by this afternoon, though mid to upper level clouds 
from convective blowoff from the southwest will arrive just in time 
to keep us partly to mostly cloudy thereafter. Some sunshine may try 
to work its way in in some of the wider valleys. All in all, today 
will be a quiet, tranquil day. 

Winds will turn more southerly today as high pressure nudges north 
from the Mid-Atlantic. This will usher in a much more milder air 
mass as temperatures warm into the low 70s today, and into the low 
to mid 70s by Thursday. Complicating our maximum temperature 
potential Thursday, however, will be the presence of advected low 
level moisture and potential shower activity, described in key 
message 2. Humidity will also be on the increase as Pacific tropical 
moisture from the southwest advects to the northeast along a frontal 
system by the late week. Dewpoints will increase to around 60 
degrees by Thursday afternoon.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A brief pattern change will take place by the latter 
portion of the week as shower chances and warmer temperatures return 
to the region, associated with Pacific tropical air. Zonal flow 
Thursday will turn more amplified to the southwest by Friday, 
advecting warm air and higher dewpoints in the region.  Decent 
isentropic lift along an approaching warm front in the St. Lawrence 
Valley will spur shower chances by Thursday afternoon. Trends 
continue to support at least some isolated shower chances in 
northern New York during the day Thursday, though the GFS continues 
to hold precipitation across the border in Ontario until closer to 
Friday morning. Regardless, by Friday morning, a cold front will 
push through the region with elevated PWs up to 1.5-1.8"; more 
reminiscent of a summer-time airmass. Thankfully, this front will be 
quite progressive, aided by a 50-60kt LLJ, and good stretching 
between a Bermuda high, and a building high across the Midwest. As a 
result, ensembles depict only a couple tenths of an inch of rain, 
mainly across northern New York and the spine of the Greens in 
Vermont. Only a 10-20% chance of exceeding 1" of rain exists in the 
GEFS and Euro ensembles, and is focused only over the St. Lawrence 
Valley. There are no indications for heavy rain, though warm rain 
processes will support downpours and locally higher rainfall 
amounts.

As our flow pattern turns more southwesterly on Thursday, our 
gradient flow will also tighten with localized gusty winds expected. 
Soundings depict gusty channeled flow in the Champlain Valley winds 
with reasonable winds in the 25-30+ MPH range. Across northern New 
York, slightly stronger channeled flow is expected with winds in the 
northern St. Lawrence Valley in locations like Malone, NY, 
approaching 35 MPH out ahead of the cold front during the day 
Thursday. Given climatology, sustained winds look marginally strong 
in this area but gusts will not be impactful. Mountain summits will 
likely remain gusty around 40 MPH Thursday through mid day Friday. 
Winds look to weaken through the day Friday as the frontal system 
continues to track east.

Behind the cold front, Friday night, clouds will clear from west to 
east towards sunrise Saturday with the potential for climo favored 
valley fog and seasonably cool temperatures overnight. However, 
winds will remain fairly breezy, complicating the fog forecast. 
Temperatures may approach 40 in the higher terrain and in the 30s 
for the ADKs and portions of the NEK overnight Friday.

KEY MESSAGE 3: As has been the case since August, pretty much being 
dictated by northern stream flow with varying amplitudes and 
strengths of disturbances. 

A northern stream shortwave and surface low track across Ontario and 
Quebec Sunday night-Monday with a chance of showers, especially 
northern sections and much cooler air on its heels. By Tuesday 
morning lows will be in the 20s-30s with highs in the 50s with some 
upper 40s as well.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 12Z Thursday...aT 12Z, Conditions remain a mix of VFR-
IFR across the area based on the height of the stratus layer. 
Gradual improvement is likely, and most locations should be near
or at VFR conditions after 18z. Increasing mid clouds and a 
southwest gradient should keep VFR for tonight in NY but some
patchy fog possible from eastern slopes of the Green mountains
eastward.

Outlook...

Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Friday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$

air.discussion: Expect generally good air quality across Vermont on Wednesday, September 30th.  Note, however, that fine particulate matter (PM25), may register in the moderate range on an hourly basis during the morning hours on Wednesday in portions of the Champlain Valley, but the 24 hour average is expected to remain in the 'good' range.
